entries.name: Roy Lisker

expected.charges: Destruction of a Selective Service registration certificate (the November 6, 1965 Union Square, NYC draft-card burning).
expected.convicted: Three of the five (Cornell, Edelman, Lisker) were convicted — United States v. Edelman — and sentenced to six months.

updates.sentence: Six-month sentence for the 1965 draft-card protest; served in 1972. His first-person account describes four and a half months after good-time reduction, while his photographic autobiography rounds the term to five months. Incarceration dates are recorded at month precision.

entries.rationale: Personal photographic autobiography explicitly identifies August-December 1972 federal custody. His first-person Hitch-hiking account independently specifies December 1972 release and four-and-a-half months after good time. Do not convert rounded months to exact days, infer arrest from the November 1965 protest, or treat appellate proceedings as continuous imprisonment.
